spiritual_reading: The love that is active and openly felt in the natural degree performs a sufficient set of operations in the human. First, it consumes and disperses what is merely natural and dead, together with whatever is adjoined to that state, so that such things can no longer rule. Second, it distinguishes and brings into order the components within that natural state, setting apart what can be elevated into love and wisdom from what must fall away into what is rejected and what is merely persuasive appearance. Third, it imparts an inner quality to the uses that are being formed through it, making them delightful and acceptable as they come into effect; and it also communicates vivifying warmth and gladness to those who are in conjunction with it. Fourth, it enables all who are in the disciplines of use to form the containing structures of life, so that the powers of the mind can be shaped into instruments for service through that love. Fifth, it manifests wisdom in an outward way, so that people are able to perceive and discern in the natural degree by means of it.
assessment: Both lacunae are trivial and syntactically fixed: the fourth and fifth works are predicated of the same subject introduced in ¶1 (“This fire”), so the pronoun must be restored as “it” in each case. No alternative reading better fits the correspondential structure, which maintains one agent (active love in the natural degree) performing five operations.
